subject.title: [Bug]: GitHub Copilot anthropic-messages transport silently hangs ~365s in isolated cron sessions (2026.5.27)

question: For GitHub Copilot Claude cron runs that idle-timeout or abort with no assistant text, should OpenClaw add side-effect-safe model fallback beyond the current cron error status and 60-second idle cap?
rationale: The remaining behavior is not purely mechanical: retrying can recover message delivery, but current replay metadata shows fallback can repeat side effects if tools or outbound actions already happened.

options.title: Prove first, fallback narrowly
options.body: Run live current-main Copilot cron proof and allow fallback only when no tool, message, spawn, or cron side-effect evidence exists.

options.title: Fallback on no-output aborts
options.body: Classify aborted or no-output Copilot results as fallback-worthy whenever a fallback model is configured, accepting the replay risk.

options.title: Do not expand fallback
options.body: Keep current-main cron error surfacing and the 60-second idle cap without adding a new aborted-result fallback path.

recommendation.title: Prove first, fallback narrowly
recommendation.body: Run live current-main Copilot cron proof and allow fallback only when no tool, message, spawn, or cron side-effect evidence exists.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history across the Copilot Claude transport and provider/runtime stream seams where this policy would land.
